title: Pahlavi Texts, Part III: Dina-i Mainog-i Khirad, Sikand-Gumanik Vigar and Sad Dar
transliteration: Dēnkard III, Šikand-gumānīg wizār, Sad Dar
dateDisplay: 9th century CE; the Sad Dar is a later compilation (c. 16th century)
attributionNote: The Mainog-i Khirad and the Sikand-Gumanik Vigar are anonymous ninth-century Pahlavi works. The Sad Dar is a later Middle Persian/New Persian compendium of religious law; none is ascribed to a named author.
description: The third volume of West's series contains the Dina-i Mainog-i Khirad, a dialogue in sixty-three chapters in which the soul of wisdom answers questions on the origin of evil, the nature of the world, fate, sin and salvation; the Sikand-Gumanik Vigar, a systematic refutation of Judaism, Christianity, Islam, Manichaeism and other religions; and the Sad Dar, one hundred chapters of Zoroastrian law and custom.
historicalContext: These are the principal theological and apologetic works of ninth-century Zoroastrianism, written when the community was a minority under Islamic rule. The Sad Dar, added in this volume, is a later summary of the same legal tradition. E. W. West translated the volume for the Sacred Books of the East (volume 24, 1885).
availabilityNote: Complete for this volume. The Mainog-i Khirad (63 chapters), the Sikand-Gumanik Vigar (16 chapters) and the Sad Dar (100 chapters) are streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one chapter per page. The volume's introduction and editorial observations are not part of the work.
